ZH-HSK2-01-001.notes: 过 after the verb marks experience: it happened at some point up to now, with no time specified. The result needn't still hold, so 我去过北京 implies I'm not there now.

ZH-HSK2-01-002.notes: 过 + 吗 asks about experience: 'have you ever…?'. The short answers are 吃过 and 没吃过, and the A-not-A form is 你吃没吃过?

ZH-HSK2-01-003.notes: The negative of experiential 过 keeps 过: 没 + verb + 过. That's the opposite of 了, which disappears under 没. 从来没…过 strengthens it to 'never once'.

ZH-HSK2-01-004.notes: No time word and the point is experience → 过; 昨天 pins down one occasion → 了. A time word can go with 过 only when it marks a period: 去年我去过两次.
ZH-HSK2-01-004.tip: A specific past moment (昨天, 上周三) normally rules out 过.

ZH-HSK2-01-005.notes: Here 过 is completion rather than experience: 吃过饭了 = I've already eaten, the usual answer to an invitation to eat. Final 了 confirms the current state.

ZH-HSK2-01-006.notes: A past event is negated with 没, and 了 drops: 他没来, never 他没来了. 上周 sets the time; the verb itself never changes form.
ZH-HSK2-01-006.text: 他上周{{c1::没来::didn't come (no 了)}}上课。
ZH-HSK2-01-006.tr: He didn't come to class last week.
ZH-HSK2-01-006.flag: dup: replaced 我昨天没去 (repeated in HSK1-06-001); answer 没去 → 没来

ZH-HSK2-01-007.notes: 开 + 着 describes the resulting state (open), not the act of opening. 门开了 would report the change: the door has just opened.

ZH-HSK2-01-008.notes: 穿 + 着 describes what she has on, a state; 她在穿衣服 would be the act of getting dressed. Verbs of wearing (穿, 戴) are among the commonest with 着.

ZH-HSK2-01-009.notes: In V1 着 + V2, the first verb gives the manner of the second: reading in a lying position. Common pairs are 站着吃, 走着去 and 笑着说.

ZH-HSK2-01-010.notes: Place + verb + 着 + thing is the existence pattern: the map is in a hanging state on the wall. The thing is new information, so it takes number + measure word (张 for flat objects).

ZH-HSK2-01-011.notes: 正在 stresses that the action is under way at this very moment, which makes it a natural excuse for not doing something else. It can't go with verbs of state: 正在知道 is impossible.

ZH-HSK2-01-012.notes: 正在 and final 呢 often frame the action together, though either would do alone. 开会 is a verb + object compound, so 正在 goes before the whole thing.

ZH-HSK2-01-013.notes: An action under way takes 在 before the verb; 着 after a verb describes a resulting state or the manner of another action. 洗澡 leaves no lasting state, so 洗着澡 only works as background: 洗着澡唱歌.
ZH-HSK2-01-013.tip: 着 marks a state (门开着); 在 + verb marks an action in progress.

ZH-HSK2-02-001.notes: 完 shows the action reached its end: the whole book has been read. Without it, 我看了这本书 says only that some reading took place.

ZH-HSK2-02-002.notes: 懂 marks understanding achieved: 听懂 by listening, 看懂 by reading. 听 alone is just the act of listening, with no guarantee of success.

ZH-HSK2-02-003.notes: 见 marks perception achieved: 看 is to look, 看见 is to see, just as 听 / 听见 are listen / hear. 看到 is a common alternative to 看见.

ZH-HSK2-02-004.notes: 到 marks reaching a goal: 找 is to look for, 找到 is to find. Many verbs take 到 for success: 买到, 收到, 想到.

ZH-HSK2-02-005.notes: 好 marks a task completed properly and now ready for use. 饭做好了 is the standard call to the table; 做完了 would say only that the cooking has stopped.

ZH-HSK2-02-006.notes: 错 marks an action done wrongly: 写错, 说错, 走错 (go the wrong way), 打错 (dial a wrong number). Its counterpart is 对 (写对了), and the negative is 没写错.

ZH-HSK2-02-007.notes: Result complements are negated with 没, not 不, and 了 drops: 没听懂. The form with 不 inside (听不懂) is a different structure, the potential complement.
ZH-HSK2-02-007.tip: 没听懂 = didn't understand (this time); 听不懂 = can't understand.

ZH-HSK2-02-008.notes: 得 links the verb 唱 to a comment on how well it's done. The comment is usually an adjective with a degree word: 唱得很好, 唱得不错.

ZH-HSK2-02-009.notes: With an object (汉语), the verb is repeated before 得: 说汉语说得…. The first 说 is often dropped, giving the usual form of this compliment: 你汉语说得真好.

ZH-HSK2-02-010.notes: After 得, a bare adjective tends to sound comparative (跑得快 = faster than others), so a plain statement adds a degree word: 很快, 非常快.

ZH-HSK2-02-011.notes: In a degree complement the negative goes after 得: 睡得不好, never 不睡得好. 昨天 covers the previous night here.

ZH-HSK2-02-012.notes: Before a noun (书) → 的; after a verb (写), introducing a comment on manner → 得. Both are pronounced de, so only the character shows the function.

ZH-HSK2-02-013.notes: A modifying adjective phrase (很漂亮) needs 的 before the noun. Only single-syllable adjectives attach directly: 红衣服, 好朋友.

ZH-HSK2-02-014.notes: 得 follows the verb 做 and introduces the evaluation; this is the standard way to praise someone's work. The noun-like 你做的 (what you made) would need a different predicate.
ZH-HSK2-02-014.tip: 做的很好 for 做得很好 is a very common slip in informal writing.

ZH-HSK2-02-015.notes: Direction is judged from the speaker: coming in towards someone inside → 进来; going out away from them → 出去. The complement is unstressed and often neutral-toned (jìnlai).

ZH-HSK2-02-016.notes: The speaker is at home, so returning home is movement towards them: 回来. 下班 (finish work) is a verb + object compound, followed by the movement 回来.
ZH-HSK2-02-016.text: (The speaker is at home) 爸爸下班回{{c1::来::来 or 去?}}了。
ZH-HSK2-02-016.flag: dup: replaced 你什么时候回来

ZH-HSK2-02-017.notes: From downstairs, coming down means moving towards the speaker: 下来. 快 before a verb in a command means 'hurry up and…'.

ZH-HSK2-03-001.notes: The duration (两年) can sit between the verb and the object, like a measure phrase: 学了两年汉语. 两 is used because 年 behaves like a measure word.

ZH-HSK2-03-002.notes: Duration goes after the verb (睡了八个小时), never before it. 小时 needs 个, but 天, 年 and 分钟 don't: 八天, 两年. 钟头 is a colloquial northern alternative to 小时.

ZH-HSK2-03-003.notes: With a pronoun object (你), the duration follows the pronoun: 等了你半个小时. 半个小时 has 半 before the measure word because there's no whole number.

ZH-HSK2-03-004.notes: Repeating the verb fits both object and duration: 学汉语 + 学了三年. With no final 了 this reports a finished period; 学了三年了 would mean the study is still going on.
ZH-HSK2-03-004.tr: I studied Chinese for three years.
ZH-HSK2-03-004.flag: tr: without a final 了 the sentence doesn't say the learning is still going on; was 'I've been learning'

ZH-HSK2-03-005.notes: The double 了 (verb + 了 … duration + 了) means the situation has lasted that long and continues. With only the first 了, 住了十年 would be over: I lived here for ten years.
ZH-HSK2-03-005.text: 我在这儿住了十年{{c1::了::still going (sentence-final)}}。
ZH-HSK2-03-005.tr: I've lived here for ten years (and still do).
ZH-HSK2-03-005.flag: dup: replaced 我学中文学了三年了 (same as HSK3-08-018)

ZH-HSK2-03-006.notes: 开车 is a verb + object compound, so the verb is repeated to carry the duration: 开车开了五个小时. Splitting the compound is the alternative: 开了五个小时车.
ZH-HSK2-03-006.text: 他开车{{c1::开了::drive (repeated verb + 了)}}五个小时。
ZH-HSK2-03-006.flag: dup: replaced 他学汉语学了三年 (same as HSK2-03-004); answer 学了 → 开了

ZH-HSK2-03-007.notes: A pronoun object stays next to the verb, before the duration: 等了他半天. 半天 is literally 'half a day' but usually just means 'ages'.

ZH-HSK2-03-008.notes: 次 counts occasions. With a place-name object it can go either side (去过中国两次 or 去过两次中国); with a pronoun object it must come after the pronoun.

ZH-HSK2-03-009.notes: 遍 counts complete run-throughs, start to finish, which suits watching a whole film. The object 这个电影 is moved to the front as topic, leaving 看了三遍.

ZH-HSK2-03-010.notes: Asking someone to repeat what they said takes 遍, because the whole utterance is to be said again. 再 marks repetition still to come.

ZH-HSK2-03-011.notes: A pronoun object (他) comes before the frequency: 见过他两次. With a noun object both orders are possible.
ZH-HSK2-03-011.tip: 见过两次他 is wrong: the pronoun goes before the frequency.

ZH-HSK2-03-012.notes: 下 counts quick, brief actions such as knocks, taps and claps. Here the frequency goes before the noun object 门.

ZH-HSK2-03-013.notes: 趟 counts round trips, there and back, so it's the natural measure word for errands. 次 would simply count occasions.

ZH-HSK2-03-014.notes: 一下 after the verb makes the action brief and the request politer. 等一下 is also a stock phrase for 'hang on'.

ZH-HSK2-03-015.notes: 一下 softens the instruction; 你看这个 without it sounds abrupt. With an object, 一下 comes between the verb and the object.

ZH-HSK2-03-016.notes: Reduplicating a one-syllable verb (试试) means 'have a go'; 试一试 and 试一下 are near-equivalents. The second syllable is usually neutral-toned.

ZH-HSK2-03-017.notes: Two-syllable verbs reduplicate as ABAB (休息休息), not AABB. Only action verbs reduplicate; states like 知道 or 喜欢 don't.

ZH-HSK2-03-018.notes: With 了, a reduplicated verb becomes V了V: 想了想, a brief completed action. It typically leads into a second action, as here.
ZH-HSK2-03-018.text: 他想{{c1::了想::thought briefly (V了V)}}，还是同意了。
ZH-HSK2-03-018.tr: He thought for a moment, then agreed.
ZH-HSK2-03-018.flag: dup: replaced 他看了看我 (flagged against HSK2-02-003 我看见他了); answer 了看 → 了想

ZH-HSK2-03-019.notes: ABAB reduplication of a two-syllable verb (研究研究) makes the action tentative. 研究研究 is also a stock official phrase, sometimes heard as a polite way of putting something off.

ZH-HSK2-04-001.notes: 比 + B comes before the adjective, so English 'colder than yesterday' becomes 比昨天冷. A (今天) is the topic and leads the sentence.

ZH-HSK2-04-002.notes: The adjective in a 比 sentence stands bare: 很, 非常 and 太 are all ruled out. To intensify, add 得多 or 多了 after it: 他比我高得多.
ZH-HSK2-04-002.tip: 他比我很高 is a classic error.

ZH-HSK2-04-003.notes: The size of the difference goes after the adjective: 大三岁, 高十厘米. For age, 大 and 小 (not 老 / 年轻) say who's older.

ZH-HSK2-04-004.notes: 一点儿 after the adjective gives a small difference, and 儿 is often dropped outside the north (贵一点). It can't go before the adjective: 比那个一点儿贵 is wrong.

ZH-HSK2-04-005.notes: 更 goes before the adjective (unlike 一点儿, which follows) and implies the other book is interesting too. 那本 drops 书, since the noun is understood.

ZH-HSK2-04-006.notes: 还 in a 比 sentence means 'even', presupposing that B already has the quality to a notable degree (the older brother is tall). It's more emphatic and more colloquial than 更.
ZH-HSK2-04-006.text: 弟弟比哥哥{{c1::还::even (比 … + adj)}}高。
ZH-HSK2-04-006.tr: The younger brother is even taller than the older one.
ZH-HSK2-04-006.flag: dup: replaced 今天比昨天还冷 (near-identical to HSK2-04-001)

ZH-HSK2-04-007.notes: A 没有 B + adjective means A falls short of B, and implies B has the quality to a notable degree (Beijing is cold). The adjective again takes no 很.
ZH-HSK2-04-007.text: 上海{{c1::没有::not as … as (negative comparison)}}北京冷。
ZH-HSK2-04-007.tr: Shanghai isn't as cold as Beijing.
ZH-HSK2-04-007.flag: dup: replaced 我没有他高 (flagged against 他比我高)

ZH-HSK2-04-008.notes: 没有 is the usual negative of a 比 comparison. 今天不比昨天热 also exists but means something else: today is no hotter than yesterday.
ZH-HSK2-04-008.tip: 不比 means 'no more … than', not 'not as … as'.

ZH-HSK2-04-009.notes: A 跟 B 一样 states sameness, and 你的 stands for 你的手机. 和 and the more formal 同 can replace 跟 in this frame.
ZH-HSK2-04-009.text: 我的手机{{c1::跟::with (not 和; … 一样)}}你的一样。
ZH-HSK2-04-009.flag: hint: 和 fitted equally; added (not 和)

ZH-HSK2-04-010.notes: An adjective after 一样 gives 'as … as': 一样漂亮. The negative of this is usually expressed with 没有 (没有她妈妈漂亮) rather than 不一样漂亮.

ZH-HSK2-04-011.notes: 那么 (or 这么) after 没有 B adds 'so / that': not as tall as you are. It strengthens the comparison but is optional.

ZH-HSK2-04-012.notes: A 跟 B 不一样 = different from. The negative goes before 一样, not before 跟: 南方菜不跟北方菜一样 is unidiomatic. 不同 is the more written equivalent of 不一样.
ZH-HSK2-04-012.text: 南方菜{{c1::跟::with (not 和; … 北方菜不一样)}}北方菜不一样。
ZH-HSK2-04-012.tr: Southern food is different from northern food.
ZH-HSK2-04-012.flag: dup: replaced 我的看法跟你不一样 (near-identical frame to HSK2-04-009); hint adds (not 和)

ZH-HSK2-04-013.notes: 最 picks one out of a whole group (我们班); 更 compares two. 最 + adjective + 的 works as a noun phrase: 最高的 (the tallest one).

ZH-HSK2-04-014.notes: 最 also modifies verbs of feeling: 最喜欢 = like best, here out of all seasons. 更喜欢 would compare just two options, like English 'prefer'.

ZH-HSK2-05-001.notes: 是 + 不 + 是 makes the question, with no 吗. 是不是 can also be tagged on to check an assumption: 你是学生，是不是?

ZH-HSK2-05-002.notes: A-not-A with a one-syllable verb doubles it around 不: 去不去, with 不 neutral-toned in fast speech. The time word 明天 stays before the verb.

ZH-HSK2-05-003.notes: A two-syllable adjective can do A-not-A in full (好吃不好吃) or clipped (好不好吃); the clipped form is more common in speech.

ZH-HSK2-05-004.notes: 有 is negated with 没, so its A-not-A form is 有没有. 有没有 + verb also asks whether something happened (你有没有看见他?), a pattern established in the south and Taiwan and spreading north.

ZH-HSK2-05-005.notes: For a past event, A-not-A uses 没: 去没去 (did you go or not?). 你昨天去了没有? is the more common alternative.

ZH-HSK2-05-006.notes: 还是 offers alternatives in a question (choose one); 或者 lists them in a statement (either will do). 都可以 in the second line confirms it's a statement.

ZH-HSK2-05-007.notes: A suggestion with 吧 is a statement, not a question, so 或者. 还是 would turn it into 'Saturday or Sunday?'.

ZH-HSK2-05-008.notes: A choice question takes 还是, with the second option (打车) following directly. 吗 is never added to a 还是 question.
ZH-HSK2-05-008.text: 你坐地铁{{c1::还是::还是 or 或者?}}打车？
ZH-HSK2-05-008.tr: Are you taking the underground or a taxi?
ZH-HSK2-05-008.flag: dup: replaced 你是中国人还是日本人 (flagged against HSK1-03-001)

ZH-HSK2-05-009.notes: 为什么 asks for a reason and goes before the verb, after the subject. Answers usually start with 因为; 为啥 is a colloquial northern variant of 为什么.

ZH-HSK2-05-010.notes: 怎么 + a negative or unexpected situation expresses surprise (how come…?) rather than asking for a method. 为什么 would be a neutral request for the reason.

ZH-HSK2-05-011.notes: 怎么 + verb asks for the method; 怎么走 is the standard request for directions. 怎么去 would ask about the means of transport instead.

ZH-HSK2-05-012.notes: 怎么 + 这么 + adjective expresses surprise or complaint: how come it's so…? 这么 points to the situation at hand, 那么 to something further away.

ZH-HSK2-05-013.notes: 怎么了 asks what has happened or what's wrong, and stands as the whole predicate. Here it's about the child; to the person themselves it's 你怎么了?
ZH-HSK2-05-013.text: 孩子一直在哭，他{{c1::怎么了::what's wrong}}？
ZH-HSK2-05-013.tr: The child keeps crying — what's wrong with him?
ZH-HSK2-05-013.flag: dup: replaced 你怎么了 (flagged against 你怎么又忘了)

ZH-HSK2-06-001.notes: 是…的 focuses on a detail of a known past event, here the time. 是 goes right before the focused element (什么时候), and 的 closes the sentence.

ZH-HSK2-06-002.notes: The focus is the means of travel (坐飞机). The arrival itself is presupposed, so 了 isn't used. 坐 + vehicle comes before 来, as the first of two serial verbs.
ZH-HSK2-06-002.tip: No 了 in 是…的: 我是坐飞机来的, not …来了.

ZH-HSK2-06-003.notes: Place of birth is the classic 是…的 case: the birth is presupposed and the place is the news. In speech 是 can be dropped: 他在北京出生的.

ZH-HSK2-06-004.notes: The focus here is the companion. When the verb has an object, 的 often moves in front of it: 我是昨天买的票.

ZH-HSK2-06-005.notes: 要…了 signals something imminent; 快, 快要 and 就要 are near-equivalents. Of these, only 就要 can combine with a specific time word.
ZH-HSK2-06-005.text: 火车{{c1::要::about to (one character, not 快)}}开了。
ZH-HSK2-06-005.flag: hint: 快 / 快要 / 就要 all fitted; added (one character, not 快)

ZH-HSK2-06-006.notes: 快 + time + 了 = it's nearly…. Unlike 要, 快 goes comfortably straight before a number or time: 快十二点了, 快三十岁了, 快过年了.
ZH-HSK2-06-006.text: {{c1::快::nearly (one character, not 要)}}十二点了。
ZH-HSK2-06-006.flag: hint: 快要 also fitted; added (one character, not 要)

ZH-HSK2-06-007.notes: With a definite time word (明天), 就要 is required; 快要 can't take one. 就 here adds a sense of 'as soon as that'.
ZH-HSK2-06-007.tip: 他明天快要走了 is wrong: 快要 can't take a time word.

ZH-HSK2-06-008.notes: Serial verbs follow the order of events: go to the shop, then buy. The second verb (买) expresses the purpose with no linking word.

ZH-HSK2-06-009.notes: The first verb phrase (坐地铁) is the means, the second the main action. 坐 is for any vehicle you ride inside; 骑 for bikes and horses.

ZH-HSK2-06-010.notes: 去 + place comes first, then the purpose (看书); 来 works the same way (来北京学习). A time word like 每天 goes before the whole chain.
ZH-HSK2-06-010.text: 他每天{{c1::去::go (first verb)}}图书馆看书。
ZH-HSK2-06-010.tr: He goes to the library every day to read.
ZH-HSK2-06-010.flag: dup: replaced 我们去饭店吃饭吧 (near-identical to HSK1-08-003)

ZH-HSK2-06-011.notes: 让 + person + verb is a pivot sentence: 我 is the object of 让 and the subject of 回家. 让 covers 'let', 'make' and 'tell', and context decides which.
ZH-HSK2-06-011.text: 妈妈{{c1::让::let / make / tell (not 叫)}}我早点儿回家。
ZH-HSK2-06-011.flag: hint: 叫 fitted equally; added (not 叫)

ZH-HSK2-06-012.notes: 叫 + person + verb = tell someone to do something. It's more colloquial than 让 and leans towards an instruction.
ZH-HSK2-06-012.text: 老师{{c1::叫::tell (someone to do; not 让)}}我们写作业。
ZH-HSK2-06-012.flag: hint: 让 fitted equally; added (not 让)

ZH-HSK2-06-013.notes: 不让 + person + verb = not let someone do something. Where the negative goes matters: 让他不去 would mean 'tell him not to go'.

ZH-HSK2-07-001.notes: 应该 gives advice or obligation and comes before the verb phrase. 早点儿 (a bit earlier) is an adverbial before 睡.

ZH-HSK2-07-002.notes: This 得 is read děi, the colloquial 'have to', and 了 marks the new situation (it's got late). It has no direct negative: 'don't have to' is 不用.

ZH-HSK2-07-003.notes: 敢 (dare) is a modal verb and comes before the main verb. Its negative 不敢 is far more frequent than the positive.

ZH-HSK2-07-004.notes: The request with 你…帮我吗 asks about willingness, so 愿意, a polite way of asking without imposing. On its own, 我愿意 is the 'I do' of Chinese wedding vows.

ZH-HSK2-07-005.notes: The verb 谢 that follows tells you this is the reply to thanks: 不用谢, 'no need to thank'. Alternatives are 不客气 (neutral), 没事儿 (casual, northern) and 不谢 (brief).

ZH-HSK2-07-006.notes: 不要 + verb gives a prohibition or warning, with 别 as its shorter equivalent. In signs and classroom rules, 不要 is more usual than 别.

ZH-HSK2-07-007.notes: 得 (děi) has no grammatical negative: 不得 means 'must not' in formal rules. 'Don't have to' is 不用, or 不必 in more formal style.

ZH-HSK2-07-008.notes: The cue is a past occasion, and 能 negated for the past is 没能 (didn't manage to). 不能去 would mean 'can't go', about now or the future.

ZH-HSK2-08-001.notes: 再 is for repetition still to come (a future plan or a request); 又 for repetition that has already happened. 又 also covers predictable repeats: 明天又是星期一了.

ZH-HSK2-08-002.notes: The forgetting has already happened again, so 又, and with 怎么 it sounds reproachful. 又 usually comes with 了.

ZH-HSK2-08-003.notes: 下次 sets the meeting in the future, so 再. The everyday goodbye 再见 is literally 'see again', with the same future 再.

ZH-HSK2-08-004.notes: 再 also means 'and only then': do A first, then B. The first action takes 了 (吃了饭), and 再 introduces the delayed second one.

ZH-HSK2-08-005.notes: 就 marks earlier or sooner than expected and goes with 了; 才 marks later than expected, and its sentence takes no 了. The time word comes before both.
ZH-HSK2-08-005.tip: 才 takes no 了: 他十点才起床, not …才起床了.

ZH-HSK2-08-006.notes: 就 here means 'soon': 一会儿就 = in a moment. It refers to the future, so there's no 了, and 回来 (not 回去) because the speaker will return to where they are now.

ZH-HSK2-08-007.notes: 才 after the time word (现在) signals lateness, and 怎么 turns it into a complaint. As always with this 才, the sentence takes no 了.

ZH-HSK2-08-008.notes: 才 before a number means 'only', a small amount. The verb can be dropped with prices and ages: 才五十 (块).

ZH-HSK2-08-009.notes: 才 + time = only, earlier than you'd think. It's the opposite of 已经七点了 (it's already seven), and here too 才 rules out 了.

ZH-HSK2-08-010.notes: 就 before a noun singles it out: only he. 只有他一个人没来 is the neutral equivalent; 一个人 here means 'alone, the single one', not 'a person'.

ZH-HSK2-08-011.notes: Pointing emphatically at a place (那) calls for 就是: precisely, that very one, as when you finally arrive. Without 就, 那是我家 is a plain statement.

ZH-HSK2-08-012.notes: 还 + 在 + verb = still doing. Its negative counterpart, 还没, means 'not yet': 他还没起床. 睡觉 is the activity of sleeping; 睡着 is falling asleep.

ZH-HSK2-08-013.notes: 已经 presupposes a reference point: the film had begun before now. Its negative counterpart is 还没 (开始), which drops 了.
ZH-HSK2-08-013.flag: dup: replaced 我已经吃饭了 (same meaning and translation as HSK2-01-005 我吃过饭了)

ZH-HSK2-08-014.notes: 还 adds another item, 'also, in addition', and goes before the second verb (还买了), not before the object.

ZH-HSK2-08-015.notes: 在等你 is an ongoing action, and the meaning is that it hasn't stopped: 一直, all along. It combines naturally with 在 + verb, unlike 总是, which is about repeated occasions.

ZH-HSK2-08-016.notes: 我…来 with no time word is a promise about the next moment, so 马上 (right away). 马上就来 is the common fuller form; it's what staff say when you call them over.

ZH-HSK2-08-017.notes: 还 + 行 / 可以 / 不错 = fairly, passable. It's a lukewarm verdict, weaker than 不错 alone, and a polite way to avoid real praise.

ZH-HSK2-08-018.notes: 别 is the one-character equivalent of 不要 and sounds more immediate in speech. It's used only for prohibitions, never in statements: 我别去 is wrong.
ZH-HSK2-08-018.flag: hint: 不要 fitted equally; added (one character)

ZH-HSK2-08-019.notes: With 你 as subject, 别 still gives an instruction, here as reassurance. 不用担心 is a near-synonym that sounds less like an order.
ZH-HSK2-08-019.flag: hint: 不要 fitted equally; added (one character)

ZH-HSK2-08-020.notes: 只 goes before the verb (只有), not before the noun as English 'only ten yuan' might suggest. 只 + 有 is its commonest pattern.

ZH-HSK2-08-021.notes: 只 + verb restricts what follows: only water, nothing else. To restrict the subject you need 只有: 只有他喝水 (only he drinks water).

ZH-HSK2-09-001.notes: 从…到… sets a time span, and the whole span goes before the verb (上课); English puts it after. 从 can drop in speech: 八点到十二点上课.

ZH-HSK2-09-002.notes: With places, 从…到… marks a route. 要 + time here means 'takes', and 几个小时 asks the number of hours with 几 because the answer is small.

ZH-HSK2-09-003.notes: 从 + place marks origin; inside 是…的 it asks where someone comes from. 你是哪国人? asks nationality more directly.

ZH-HSK2-09-004.notes: 离 marks the reference point for distance, and the predicate is 远 or 近 with a degree word. The subject (我家) is what's being placed.
ZH-HSK2-09-004.tip: Not 从: 我家从学校很近 is a common error.

ZH-HSK2-09-005.notes: The predicate of a 离 sentence is 远 or 近, or a figure: 离这儿五公里. In a 吗 question the adjective can stand bare.

ZH-HSK2-09-006.notes: 离 also measures time until an event. The sentence has no subject: 离 + event + 还有 + time. 还 stresses that the time is still to run.

ZH-HSK2-09-007.notes: 往 + direction = towards: 往前, 往左, 往北. 一直 here means 'straight on'. 向 and 朝 are near-synonyms (see HSK3).

ZH-HSK2-09-008.notes: 对 + person + attitude: kind to, strict with (对学生很严格), polite to (对客人很客气). The adjective for the attitude follows.

ZH-HSK2-09-009.notes: 给 + person introduces the recipient: call you, write to you (给你写信). The phrase goes before the verb.

ZH-HSK2-09-010.notes: 对 + thing + 好 / 不好 = good or bad for. 身体 (the body) is the usual way of saying 'for your health'; formal style has 对健康有害.

ZH-HSK2-09-011.notes: 见面 (meet) is intransitive, so the other person comes in with 跟 or 和: 跟朋友见面, never 见面朋友. 对 marks the target of an attitude or remark, not a companion.

ZH-HSK2-09-012.notes: Verb + 在 + place gives where the action leaves someone or something: 住在, 坐在, 放在, 写在. 在 before the verb (在北京工作) just sets the scene.

ZH-HSK2-09-013.notes: Verb + 给 + recipient (送给, 借给, 交给) shows the object passing to that person. 送 alone means give as a present.

ZH-HSK2-09-014.notes: Verb + 到 + place marks the endpoint reached: walked as far as the door. 走向门口 would only mean heading towards it.

ZH-HSK2-10-001.notes: 因为 introduces the cause, and Chinese happily adds 所以 as well, unlike English. Either word can also be dropped.

ZH-HSK2-10-002.notes: 所以 heads the result clause, whose subject 我 is understood from the first clause. 因为 can also come second: 我没上班，因为我病了.

ZH-HSK2-10-003.notes: 但是 introduces the contrast and starts its clause, before any subject. 很想 + verb = would really like to, the polite softening before a refusal.
ZH-HSK2-10-003.text: 我很想去，{{c1::但是::but (not 可是)}}没有时间。
ZH-HSK2-10-003.flag: hint: 可是 fitted equally; added (not 可是)

ZH-HSK2-10-004.notes: 可是 is a slightly more colloquial 'but' than 但是, and 不过 is softer still. All three start the second clause.
ZH-HSK2-10-004.text: 这件衣服很漂亮，{{c1::可是::but (not 但是)}}太贵了。
ZH-HSK2-10-004.flag: hint: 但是 fitted equally; added (not 但是)

ZH-HSK2-10-005.notes: 如果 opens the condition and 就 introduces the consequence, after the subject (我们就). Final 了 marks a change of plan.

ZH-HSK2-10-006.notes: With no subject in the result clause, 就 starts it. 来我家 is how Chinese says 'come round to mine', and 吧 makes it an invitation.

ZH-HSK2-10-007.notes: 先 is an adverb before the first verb; 然后 links the next step and can be reinforced with 再: 然后再去看电影. 去看 here is a serial verb chain.

ZH-HSK2-10-008.notes: 先 in the first clause expects a following step, introduced by 然后 (afterwards). 然后 is a conjunction, so it comes before any subject: 然后我们吃饭.

ZH-HSK2-10-009.notes: 先…再… orders two steps, and 再 is an adverb, so it comes after any subject (你再出去). It's typical of instructions to children.
ZH-HSK2-10-009.text: {{c1::先::first (… 再 …)}}把作业做完，再出去玩。
ZH-HSK2-10-009.tr: Finish your homework first, then go out and play.
ZH-HSK2-10-009.flag: dup: replaced 先洗手，再吃饭 (near-identical to HSK2-10-008)

ZH-HSK2-10-010.notes: 越来越 + adjective describes gradual change over time, with final 了 marking the change. No 很 can be added: 越来越很冷 is wrong.

ZH-HSK2-10-011.notes: 越来越 also applies to abilities, often as a compliment, with final 了 marking the change. The downward version usually uses 差: 越来越差.

ZH-HSK2-10-012.notes: 又 goes before each adjective: both cheap and tasty. The adjectives need no 很, and the two qualities are usually of the same kind, both good or both bad.

ZH-HSK2-10-013.notes: 以前 follows the clause it modifies (吃饭以前), unlike English 'before', which comes first. 要 here means 'must'.

ZH-HSK2-10-014.notes: 的时候 also follows its clause: 我小的时候 (when I was little). 小时候 is a fixed alternative without 的, and the main clause needs no 'then'.

ZH-HSK2-10-015.notes: 那 at the start, short for 那么, means 'in that case' and draws on what the other speaker has just said.

ZH-HSK2-11-001.notes: 每 + 天 needs no measure word because 天 is itself measure-like, as are 年 and 次. 都 before the verb completes the pattern.

ZH-HSK2-11-002.notes: 每 normally needs a measure word (每个人), and 都 follows before the verb; without 都 the sentence sounds unfinished.

ZH-HSK2-11-003.notes: 还要…吗 offers more of something, and 别的 (other things) fills the object slot. It's the shop assistant's 'anything else?'; 别的 can also precede a noun: 别的东西.

ZH-HSK2-11-004.notes: A greeting with 好 addressed to a group calls for 大家 (everyone present), used as a pronoun. 各位 is the more formal alternative for an audience.

ZH-HSK2-11-005.notes: 自己 after a pronoun = oneself, implying no one else does it. It also works as a reflexive object: 照顾好自己 (look after yourself).
ZH-HSK2-11-005.flag: tr: 'I cook for myself' implied 给自己; 自己做饭 means by oneself

ZH-HSK2-11-006.notes: 有的…有的… divides a group: some…, others…. It modifies the subject, so it comes before the noun; the second 人 can be dropped (有的喜欢咖啡).

ZH-HSK2-11-007.notes: 有人 + verb introduces an unspecified person. Chinese avoids indefinite subjects, so 有 brings 'someone' in.

ZH-HSK2-11-008.notes: The sentence describes an irregular habit (weekend overtime), so 有时候 (sometimes), before or after the subject. 有时 is the more written form, and 也要 means 'has to… as well'.
ZH-HSK2-11-008.tr: Sometimes he has to work at weekends too.
ZH-HSK2-11-008.flag: dup: replaced 有时候我坐地铁上班 (near-identical to HSK2-06-009)

ZH-HSK2-11-009.notes: 咱们 is the inclusive 'we' (speaker + listener), typical of northern speech; 我们 can be inclusive or exclusive.
ZH-HSK2-11-009.tr: What shall we have for dinner?
ZH-HSK2-11-009.flag: dup: replaced 咱们走吧 (same as HSK1-09-005 我们走吧)

ZH-HSK2-11-010.notes: 第 + number makes an ordinal: 第一次 (the first time). Some fixed sequences drop it: 一年级 (Year 1), 二楼 (the first floor, in British terms).

ZH-HSK2-11-011.notes: 多 after a round number gives 'more than': 四十多岁 = forty-something. With round numbers 多 comes before the measure word.
ZH-HSK2-11-011.text: 他已经四十{{c1::多::more than (… -odd)}}岁了。
ZH-HSK2-11-011.flag: dup: replaced 我们班有二十多个学生 (near-identical to HSK1-04-011)

ZH-HSK2-11-012.notes: 半 follows the measure word when added to a whole number (两个半小时) but precedes it on its own (半个小时). The time phrase here is the predicate, with no verb.
ZH-HSK2-11-012.text: 这部电影两个{{c1::半::half (after the measure word)}}小时。
ZH-HSK2-11-012.tr: This film is two and a half hours long.
ZH-HSK2-11-012.flag: dup: replaced 我等了一个半小时 (flagged against two other waiting sentences)

ZH-HSK2-11-013.notes: After 三点一, the unit for fifteen minutes is 刻: 一刻 = a quarter, 三刻 = three quarters. 两刻 isn't used, as 半 covers it, and 十五分 is more common in speech.

ZH-HSK2-11-014.notes: 差 + minutes + hour = so many minutes to: 差五分八点 = 7.55. The order (minutes before hour) is fixed. In everyday speech 七点五十五 is more common.

ZH-HSK2-11-015.notes: 几 after 十 means 'a few more': 十几 = 11 to 19. Before a ten, it multiplies instead: 几十个人 = several dozen people.

ZH-HSK2-11-016.notes: Two adjacent numbers give an estimate: 两三 (two or three), 七八 (seven or eight). No word for 'or' is needed.
ZH-HSK2-11-016.text: 我昨晚只睡了{{c1::两三::two or three}}个小时。
ZH-HSK2-11-016.tr: I only got two or three hours' sleep last night.
ZH-HSK2-11-016.flag: dup: replaced 我在北京住了两三天 (flagged against 我住在北京)

ZH-HSK2-11-017.notes: 来 after a round number means 'about', either side of it: 二十来岁 = about twenty. 二十多岁 would mean over twenty.

ZH-HSK2-11-018.notes: 有一点儿 goes before an adjective and signals mild disapproval; 一点儿 goes after one to compare or to ask for more (便宜一点儿).

ZH-HSK2-11-019.notes: 有一点儿 + adjective describes a slightly unwelcome state. In speech the short form 有点儿 is the usual one.

ZH-HSK2-11-020.notes: Adjective + 一点儿 in a request = a bit more…: 慢一点儿. The adjective follows the verb 说 here, as a complement.

ZH-HSK2-11-021.notes: 把 is the measure word for things with a handle or held in the hand: 伞, 椅子, 刀, 钥匙. It's unrelated to the 把 construction of HSK3.

ZH-HSK2-11-022.notes: 家 counts businesses and institutions: shops, restaurants, companies, hospitals. 条 counts long things such as streets.

ZH-HSK2-11-023.notes: 颜色 here are varieties, not individual items, so the measure word is 种 (kind, type). 件 counts the garment itself (这件衣服) and also matters (一件事).

ZH-HSK2-11-024.notes: 台 counts machines and appliances: 电脑, 电视, 空调, 洗衣机. 个 is also heard in casual speech, and 部 is used for phones and films.

ZH-HSK2-11-025.notes: 份 counts jobs, newspapers, copies and portions (一份饭, 一份报纸). 找到 marks success in finding, so the job has actually been secured.

ZH-HSK2-11-026.notes: 一 + measure word + noun + 也 / 都 + negative = not a single. 也 or 都 is required, and the 一 phrase goes before the verb.
